ghs.en: It means that no finished product can be delivered if there isn't some design documentation.

rows.jp: って言ったら、友貴が『プログラマーが信じそうな嘘をつくなよ』って突っ込む仕掛けだ。
rows.en: That was the setup for Tomoki to say, ‘Quit inventing lies programmers would believe.’

ghs.en: Or so I say, but that's just a setup to get Tomoki to straight-man me with a "don'tcha toss out bull that the programmers'd believe!"

rows.jp: 友貴はいいヤツだ。
rows.en: Tomoki was a good guy.

ghs.en: Tomoki's a nice guy.

rows.jp: 俺は部活が大好きだ。
rows.en: I loved our club.

ghs.en: I really love club activities.

rows.jp: 行って、今日も圧倒的な全能感に包まれてやるぞ。
rows.en: Today, too, I'd let that overwhelming sense of omnipotence wash over me. Just watch.

ghs.en: I'll go, and just watch me getting enveloped by an overwhelming feeling of omnipotence even today!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese expresses Taichi's forceful intention to go and bask in the feeling again. The English combines imperative 'watch' with a gerund where a finite future construction is required.
ghs.remedy: I'll go bask in that overwhelming sense of omnipotence again today.

rows.jp: 友貴との記憶はいくらでもある。
rows.en: I had no end of memories of Tomoki.

ghs.en: I still have a number of memories with Tomoki.
ghs.assessment: いくらでも emphasizes that he has endlessly many or as many memories as he could want. 'A number of' merely means an unspecified quantity and loses the abundance.
ghs.remedy: countless memories

rows.jp: ふたりは、桜庭を入れた三人は、いつだって楽しかったシステムを備えていたのでしたよ（†）
rows.en: The two of us—the three of us, with Sakuraba—had always come equipped with a System for Having Fun (†).

ghs.en: The two of us, and with Sakuraba that'd be the three of us, we had readied a SIStem to have fun wherever and whenever! (†)
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the pair, or trio with Sakuraba, had a system that always made things fun. The English changes possession into deliberate preparation, adds 'wherever,' and inserts unexplained internal capitalization into 'system.'
ghs.remedy: we had a system that made things fun whenever we were together

highlights.text: readied a SIStem to have fun wherever and whenever

Taichi: "............aaaaaah"

rows.jp: 『それ』が爆発しそうになった。
rows.en: ‘It’ felt ready to explode.

ghs.en: Seemed "it" was close to exploding.

rows.jp: 『それ』は『それ』としか描写できない『アレ』な『コレ』なのだ。
rows.en: ‘It’ was one of ‘those’ ‘things’ that could only be described as ‘it.’

ghs.en: "It" is of course "that" kind of "this" which cannot be described with a mere "it".

rows.jp: 『それ』は『それ』、『これ』は『これ』なのだ。
rows.en: ‘It’ was ‘it,’ and ‘this’ was ‘this.’

ghs.en: "It" is "it", "this" is "this", naturally.

rows.jp: だから呑み込む。
rows.en: So I swallowed.

ghs.en: Therefore I swallow.

rows.en: Swallow. Swallow.

rows.en: I swallowed about seven times.

ghs.en: Swallow seven times.

rows.en: Then I swallowed again.

ghs.en: And then swallow.

rows.jp: ごちそうさま。
rows.en: Thanks for the meal.

ghs.en: A most delicious meal.
ghs.assessment: ごちそうさま is the conventional expression spoken after finishing a meal, here used metaphorically after swallowing. The English replaces the speech act with a formal evaluation that the meal was delicious.
ghs.remedy: Thanks for the meal.

rows.jp: 心で叫ぶ。
rows.en: I screamed it inside my heart.

ghs.en: Shrieking in the heart.

rows.jp: 満腹だ。
rows.en: I was stuffed.

ghs.en: Belly's filled.

rows.jp: 俺の内部にあるものは、底にずっしり横たわって出てこない。
rows.en: Whatever was inside me lay heavy at the bottom and refused to come back up.

ghs.en: What exists on my inside lays heavily on the bottom and doesn't come out.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that what is inside him lies heavily at the bottom. The English uses the nonidiomatic location 'on my inside' and the transitive verb 'lays' without an object.
ghs.remedy: What is inside me lies heavily at the bottom

highlights.text: What exists on my inside lays heavily on the bottom

rows.jp: せからしか。
rows.en: What a pain in the ass.

ghs.en: What a PITA.

rows.jp: 部活は遅れがち。
rows.en: Club work was slipping behind schedule.

ghs.en: Club tends to lag behind.

rows.jp: もう金曜。
rows.en: Already Friday.

ghs.en: It's already Friday.

rows.jp: 舐・め・す・ぎ。
rows.en: I. Had. Taken. This. Way. Too. Lightly.

ghs.en: Taken! Too! Light! Ly!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese emphatically syllabifies the accusation that he has taken the work far too lightly. The English shifts into a passive past participle, splits 'lightly' at a false morphological boundary, and never identifies what was underestimated.
ghs.remedy: Way! Too! Com! Pla! Cent!

rows.jp: そこで俺は働くことにした。
rows.en: So I decided to work.

ghs.en: And therefore I decided to work.

rows.jp: 新人キャンペーンの一環として。
rows.en: As part of the rookie campaign.

ghs.en: First part of our Newman Movement.
ghs.assessment: 新人キャンペーン is a campaign or initiative for a newcomer. The English invents the proper name 'Newman Movement,' introducing both an unrelated surname and a larger organized movement.
ghs.remedy: newcomer campaign

rows.jp: 「うおー」
rows.en: “Raaah!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Woooh!"

rows.jp: 五分後、細々としたことを考えるのがイヤになってやめた。
rows.en: Five minutes later, I got sick of thinking about all the little details and quit.

ghs.en: Five minutes later, I was thinking about all and sundry and it started leaving a bad taste in my mouth so I stopped.

rows.jp: 一環の終わりだった。
rows.en: That part was over.

ghs.en: That was the end of the first part.

rows.jp: 大丈夫。二巻がある。
rows.en: No problem. There was always Part Two.

ghs.en: It's alright. There are two acts.
ghs.assessment: The joke pivots from 一環, one component, to the homophonically patterned 二巻, volume two. 'Two acts' is neither volume two nor a useful sound-based partner for the preceding 'first part.'
ghs.remedy: There's always volume two.

rows.jp: 一環が終わっても、二巻がある。
rows.en: When one part ends, Part Two begins.

ghs.en: Once the first part ends, there's the second act.
ghs.assessment: The source deliberately jumps from 'one component' to 'volume two' on the shared sound of the counters. The English makes a normal, semantically connected progression from a first part to a second act, erasing the mistake that prompts the next line.
ghs.remedy: Even when one part ends, there's volume two.

highlights.text: Once the first part ends, there's the second act.

rows.jp: おや？
rows.en: Wait.

ghs.en: Mother of---?
ghs.assessment: おや is a mild realization equivalent to 'huh?' or 'wait.' The English invents the beginning of an English curse.
ghs.remedy: Wait...?

rows.jp: 一環と二巻って繋がってないじゃないか。
rows.en: Those weren't the same kind of part at all.

ghs.en: "First part" and "second act" aren't connected are they not.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese notices that 'one component' and 'volume two' only sound connected while denoting unrelated things. The chosen English terms are in fact semantically connected, and the negative tag is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Wait, 'one part' and 'volume two' have nothing to do with each other.

highlights.text: "First part" and "second act" aren't connected are they not.

rows.jp: おかしな言葉があったものだ。
rows.en: What a strange language.

ghs.en: There were some pretty weird words there.

rows.jp: 水飛沫が空に掛けられたオレンジ色の球体を射抜く。
rows.en: A jet of water shot through the orange sphere hanging in the sky.

ghs.en: A spray of water shoots through a sphere colored orange that had been hung in the sky.

rows.jp: いや、球体ではない。
rows.en: No. Not a sphere.

ghs.en: Nope, it ain't spherical.

rows.jp: ヤツは円形かも知れない。
rows.en: Then again, maybe it was only a circle.

ghs.en: That thing might be circular, dunno.

rows.jp: 大陽平面説的な。
rows.en: The Flat-Sun Theory, or something.

ghs.en: The flat sun theory, yeah!

rows.jp: 動くもののない世界きつい。なんか出ろ。
rows.en: This world with nothing moving in it was killing me. Come on. Anything. Show yourself.

ghs.en: A world without nothing moving kills my heart. Happen, something!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese complains that a world with nothing moving is unbearable and demands that something appear. The English double negative implies that something is moving and forms the demand with reversed, ungrammatical word order.
ghs.remedy: A world with nothing moving is unbearable. Come on, something appear!

rows.jp: 大陽だけがゆるゆると移動しているが、物足りない。
rows.en: The sun alone drifted slowly along. It wasn't enough.

ghs.en: Just the sun being mobile all slowly slow is unsatisfactory.

rows.jp: ゲットできないからな。
rows.en: Couldn't catch it, for one thing.

ghs.en: Because I can't perform a GET on it.
ghs.assessment: ゲットできない uses casual loanword language for being unable to obtain or catch it. The English invents the execution of an uppercase technical operation.
ghs.remedy: get hold of it

rows.jp: ブラックホールもなれないライト級天体だしな。
rows.en: A lightweight celestial body that would never qualify for black-hole class.

ghs.en: That light-weight heavenly body can't even become a black hole.

rows.jp: 負けたって感じ。
rows.en: It felt like I'd lost.

ghs.en: It feels like it's a loser.

rows.jp: さそり座Ｖ８６１星でも見習っておけ。
rows.en: It should take lessons from V861 Scorpii.

ghs.en: Go learn something from V861 Scorpii!

rows.jp: もっとガーンと行って欲しい。
rows.en: I wanted it to go out with a bang.

ghs.en: I wish something'd happen that was much more like 'dun-dun-dunnn'.
ghs.assessment: ガーンと asks for a much more forceful, explosive impact. The English converts that impact into a musical dramatic-sting sound effect.
ghs.remedy: go out with a much bigger bang

rows.jp: あと白色矮星見たい。
rows.en: Also, I wanted to see a white dwarf.

ghs.en: And I wanna see a white dwarf.

rows.jp: 確か桜庭が。
rows.en: Sakuraba, if I remembered right.

ghs.en: I'm sure Sakuraba has.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese fragment means 'if I remember right, Sakuraba...' as Taichi recalls the source of the next verbal chain. The English supplies an unsupported perfect auxiliary with no recoverable verb phrase.
ghs.remedy: If I remember right, Sakuraba once...

rows.jp: 役不足を感じた確信犯が的を得たのだろうか。
rows.en: Had a man of conviction, feeling too big for his role, finally scored a bull’s-eye?

ghs.en: Would the premeditated crime of feeling above the role hit the target?

rows.jp: 与えられたフィールドに不満がある思想犯がアーチェリーに使われる的を手に入れた。
rows.en: A thought criminal, dissatisfied with his assigned field, had gotten his hands on an archery target.

ghs.en: Those white-collar criminals guilty of being unsatisfied with their given fields merely acquire targets for archery use.
ghs.assessment: 思想犯 means an ideological or thought criminal. The English changes the offense to financially motivated white-collar crime, pluralizes the person, and thereby breaks the continuing verbal chain.
ghs.remedy: The thought criminal dissatisfied with his assigned field obtained an archery target.

rows.jp: 俺を見てくれ。
rows.en: Look at me!

ghs.en: Look at me please.

rows.jp: あ、枝、枝！
rows.en: Oh! A branch! A branch!

ghs.en: Ah, branch, branch!

rows.en: The branch! The branch!

ghs.en: The braaanch! The braaanch!

rows.en: I destroyed the fence.

ghs.en: It destroyed the fence.

rows.jp: 架空の枝が来た！
rows.en: The imaginary branch arrived!

ghs.en: An Imaginary branch has come!

rows.jp: 見えない！
rows.en: I couldn't see it!

ghs.en: I can't see it!

rows.jp: すごい！　完璧だ！
rows.en: Amazing! Perfect!

ghs.en: Amazing! It's perfect!

rows.jp: そして落ちた！
rows.en: And then it fell!

ghs.en: And then it fell!

rows.jp: 架空の枝を地面に引き寄せる力……引く力だ！
rows.en: A force pulling the imaginary branch toward the ground... a grave matter indeed!

ghs.en: The power that draws the Air branch towards the ground... it's Pulling Power!

rows.jp: フェンスは工業用の巨大ペンチみたいので破壊した。
rows.en: For the record, I'd destroyed the fence with something like a gigantic pair of industrial cutters.

ghs.en: The fence was wrecked as if by a pair of gigantic industrial-use pliers.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi actually broke the fence with something like enormous industrial pliers. 'As if by' instead makes the pliers merely a visual comparison and removes the tool used.
ghs.remedy: with something like a gigantic pair of industrial pliers

highlights.text: as if by a pair of gigantic industrial-use pliers

rows.jp: 引力と名付けた！
rows.en: I named it gravity!

ghs.en: I shall name you Attractive Force... no, because this matter is most grave, Gravity!

rows.jp: これは大発見だ。
rows.en: A momentous discovery.

ghs.en: This is an important discovery.

rows.jp: 大航海時代のはじまりと終わり。
rows.en: The Age of Exploration—begun and ended.

ghs.en: The beginning and the end of the Age of Discovery.

rows.jp: 切断したフェンス面が、不格好に滑空していく。
rows.en: The severed fence panel sailed away, wobbling through the air.

ghs.en: The part of the fence that was cut down glides down awkwardly.

rows.jp: 無数の言葉。
rows.en: Countless words.

ghs.en: Words without number,

rows.jp: 脳を泳ぐ。
rows.en: Swimming through my brain.

ghs.en: swimming in the brain,

rows.jp: シナプス跳躍をして。
rows.en: Leaping from synapse to synapse.

ghs.en: taking the synaptic jump.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese depicts words leaping across synapses. The English turns the action into taking one definite object called 'the synaptic jump.'
ghs.remedy: leaping from synapse to synapse

rows.jp: ヤーヤー。
rows.en: Yah-yah.

ghs.en: Nooo, nooo.

rows.jp: 冬子が攻撃してきた。
rows.en: Touko attacked.

ghs.en: Touko came to attack,

rows.jp: 出会い別れそして再会という感動を挟む余地無し。
rows.en: No room for the moving drama of meeting, parting, and reunion.

ghs.en: leaving no space for the interposing the deep emotions of meeting and parting and then reuniting.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that there is no room to insert the moving sequence of meeting, separation, and reunion. The English combines 'for' with the gerund's object in an ungrammatical construction.
ghs.remedy: no room to interpose the moving sequence

highlights.text: no space for the interposing the deep emotions

rows.jp: 母親も捜せないぜ。
rows.en: I couldn't even look for my mother.

ghs.en: I can't locate Mother either.

rows.jp: 俺がしろしめしたいのは＊＊＊＊＊＊＊＊＊。
rows.en: What I wished to reign over was *********.

ghs.en: What I wanna know is how to ru*********.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese completely censors the object after 'what I want to rule.' The English exposes an uncensored semantic lead-in inside the asterisks and therefore weakens the source's total redaction.
ghs.remedy: Censor the entire redacted expression after 'what I want.'

rows.jp: そして倒した。
rows.en: Then I beat her.

ghs.en: And then she's defeated.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi then defeated her. The English removes him as agent and shifts the completed action into a present-state passive.
ghs.remedy: And then I defeated her.

rows.jp: すまん冬子！
rows.en: Sorry, Touko!

ghs.en: Sorry Touko!

rows.jp: じくり、と心が疼く。
rows.en: A slow, deep ache throbbed in my heart.

ghs.en: Squeak, and my heart aches like a living thing left out in the freezing winter.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a slow, focused throb of pain in his heart. The English invents a squeaking sound and an elaborate image of a living creature abandoned in winter.
ghs.remedy: My heart throbbed with a slow ache.

highlights.text: like a living thing left out in the freezing winter

rows.jp: 血を感じた。
rows.en: I sensed blood.

ghs.en: I felt blood.

rows.jp: 解放が必要だ。
rows.en: I needed an outlet.

ghs.en: Liberation is necessary.

rows.jp: 自分で光らないと。
rows.en: I had to shine for myself.

ghs.en: I must shine by myself.

rows.jp: 汚名を挽回すべく、俺は霧を口説く。
rows.en: To reclaim my disgrace, I set about wooing Kiri.

ghs.en: In order to redeem the stigma, I woo Kiri.

rows.jp: 名誉を返上すべく、ひたすら口説く。
rows.en: To surrender my honor, I kept right on wooing her.

ghs.en: In order to relinquish the honor, I woo earnestly.

rows.jp: 口説き抜く。
rows.en: I wooed her for all I was worth.

ghs.en: Woo continuously.

rows.jp: 高らかに口説きあげる。
rows.en: I wooed her loud and proud.

ghs.en: Raising the loudness of the wooing.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi loudly or triumphantly talks Kiri up. The English turns the action into an abstract increase in the volume level of 'the wooing.'
ghs.remedy: I woo her at the top of my lungs.

highlights.text: Raising the loudness of the wooing.

rows.jp: 申し分のないナンパ。
rows.en: Flawless pickup artistry.

ghs.en: Uncriticizable Nanpa.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls it flawless pickup or flirting. 'Uncriticizable' is unnatural evaluative English, and leaving nanpa as a capitalized unexplained loanword obscures the action.
ghs.remedy: Flawless pickup artistry.

rows.jp: しかし色よい返事はもらえない。
rows.en: But she would not give me the green light.

ghs.en: But a favorable response in good color I don't get.
ghs.assessment: 色よい返事 is an idiom for a favorable answer. The English translates the color component literally and follows Japanese word order into an ungrammatical inversion.
ghs.remedy: But I get no favorable answer.

highlights.text: a favorable response in good color I don't get

rows.jp: なぜか？
rows.en: Why?

ghs.en: How come?

rows.jp: それは霧が赤だからです。
rows.en: Because Kiri was red.

ghs.en: That would be because Kiri is scarlet.

rows.jp: 悔いる。
rows.en: Regret.

ghs.en: Regret.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is a finite action: Taichi regrets it. The English turns it into a bare abstract noun.
ghs.remedy: I regret it.

rows.jp: 畜生、畜生！
rows.en: Damn it. Damn it!

ghs.en: Fuck, fuck!

rows.jp: やらずに後悔するより、やって後悔すべきなのに！
rows.en: Better to do it and regret it than regret never doing it at all!

ghs.en: When it ought be better to regret doing than to regret not doing!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that one should regret acting rather than regret never acting. The English begins with an ungoverned 'when' clause and omits 'to' after 'ought.'
ghs.remedy: I ought to regret doing it rather than regret not doing it!

rows.jp: 一人じゃ調整できないよ。
rows.en: I couldn't tune this by myself.

ghs.en: I just can't get adjusted to being alone, you know.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the required adjustment or coordination cannot be performed by one person alone. The English instead says that Taichi cannot psychologically acclimate to solitude.
ghs.remedy: I can't make the adjustment by myself.

rows.jp: さあ霧、オラの気持ちに応えてくれ！
rows.en: Come on, Kiri! Love me back!

ghs.en: Well, Kiri, have a response to me's feelings!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese asks Kiri to respond to Taichi's feelings. The English uses 'me's' as an impossible possessive and the nonidiomatic collocation 'have a response to.'
ghs.remedy: answer my feelings

highlights.text: have a response to me's feelings

rows.jp: モノローグを駆使して俺は告った。

ghs.remedy: I confessed my feelings

ghs.en: Monologue has the meaning of speaking by oneself, however, with regards to videogame lingo, it is utilized in the nuance of descriptive and narrative text, so people who like to nitpick should start attacking that.

rows.jp: 実は告るって言葉嫌いだった。
rows.en: Truth be told, I'd never liked the phrase 'fess up.'

ghs.en: Truth is, I hated the word 'proclaim'.

rows.jp: ハンパっぽいというか。

ghs.en: Then well then.

rows.jp: モノローグを駆使して俺はギャランドゥ。
rows.en: Deploying monologue to full effect, I happy-trailed.

ghs.en: So I gyarandou'd while freely making use of monologue.

rows.jp: イカしてる。
rows.en: Stylish.

ghs.remedy: That's cool.

rows.jp: ギャラクシーって銀河っぽい単語と語感が似てるのもいい。

rows.jp: 「……フライドチキンの性別が気になりますか？」

rows.jp: あー、なる、なるってそれ！
rows.en: Oh, I am! I absolutely am!

rows.jp: じゃあ仕様がない。
rows.en: Then it can’t be specced.

ghs.en: Well, it can't be specced.

rows.jp: 手榴弾が爆発しました。
rows.en: A hand grenade exploded.

ghs.en: The flashbang had exploded.
ghs.assessment: 手榴弾 is a hand grenade. A flashbang is a distinct non-fragmentation stun device.
ghs.remedy: hand grenade

rows.jp: 俺たちは死んだ。
rows.en: We died.

ghs.en: We had died.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese simple past states that the two died as the immediate result. The English past perfect incorrectly places that death before another past reference point.
ghs.remedy: We died.

rows.jp: あなたは武器を手によく戦ったが、蠍(さそり)の数は多く、突き立てられる毒針の全てを防ぐことは不可能だ。
rows.en: You fought well, weapon in hand, but the scorpions were too numerous. You could not ward off every venomous sting.

ghs.en:
With great armed skill you fought and well, but the scorpions were so many in number that defending from the stabbing of all their poisonous stingers was impossible.
Eventually your consciousness grew faint, you collapsed, and the scorpions that submerged your body enjoyed the deliciousness of human flesh for the first time in a long while.
Your adventure has ended.

rows.jp: やがて意識が薄らぎ、倒れると、蠍たちは久方ぶりのうまい人肉に歓喜しつつあなたの体を埋め尽くした。あなたの冒険は終わった。
rows.en: At last your senses faded and you fell. Delighted by their first taste of good human flesh in ages, the scorpions swarmed over your body. Your adventure was over.

rows.jp: ウォーロック・モーロックの邪悪な計画を阻止するには、パラグラフの１に戻って冒険をやり直さなければならない。あなたの次なる冒険に、女神のじゅうぶんな加護があらんことを―――
rows.en: To thwart Warlock Morlock's evil design, you must return to paragraph one and begin your adventure anew. May the goddess grant ample protection to your next adventure—

ghs.en:
To foil the evil plan of the Warlock Morlock, you must return to Paragraph 1 and redo your adventure from the beginning.
A sufficient blessing of the Goddess in your next adventure we---
ghs.assessment: The Japanese continues with a full conventional benediction wishing the reader ample protection from the goddess on the next adventure. The English omits that entire closing sentence.
ghs.remedy: Add the omitted closing wish for the next adventure.

highlights.text: To foil the evil plan of the Warlock Morlock, you must return to Paragraph 1 and redo your adventure from the beginning.

rows.jp: なんか昔読んだ本と思考がまざったことをお詫びするよ。
rows.en: I apologize. My thoughts got mixed up with some book I read years ago.

ghs.en: I apologize for getting a book I read a long time ago mingled with my thoughts.

rows.jp: やっぱ無理があった。一人は。
rows.en: Being alone really was impossible.

ghs.en: I knew it, it's impossible. Being alone I mean.

rows.jp: ここで曜子特派員にカメラを！
rows.en: And now, to Youko, our correspondent in the field!

ghs.en: Let us turn our camera to Special Correspondent Youko!

rows.jp: おおっと、いました！
rows.en: There she is!

ghs.en: Ohmmmy, she was here!
ghs.assessment: おおっと marks a mock-presenter's sudden discovery: 'whoa, there she is.' The English invents a stretched 'oh my' and changes immediate sight into a past statement.
ghs.remedy: Whoa, there she is!

rows.jp: ばっちり見られちゃってるるる！
rows.en: Oh no—she saw every last bit of thaaat!

ghs.en: She has totally seen me-eh-eh!

rows.jp: さすが正式な訓練を受けた市原です。
rows.en: Just what one expects from a formally trained Ichihara.

ghs.en: Naught else may be expected from one who received formal Ichihara training.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese attributes the feat to formally trained Ichihara herself. The English turns her family name into a type or school of training that some unnamed person received.
ghs.remedy: Just what you'd expect from the formally trained Ichihara.

highlights.text: one who received formal Ichihara training

rows.jp: 違います。
rows.en: No.

ghs.en: That is incorrect.

rows.jp: だいぶ異なものです。
rows.en: There was something profoundly strange about her.

ghs.en: That is considerably unusual.

rows.jp: 異質です。
rows.en: Alien.

ghs.en: It is heterogeneous.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that she is qualitatively alien or different from ordinary people. 'Heterogeneous' is a technical property of a mixture and is not an idiomatic description of a person.
ghs.remedy: She's fundamentally different.

rows.jp: えーと、ごっつ優秀すぎるって感じで異質です。
rows.en: I mean freakishly, monstrously competent. That kind of strange.

ghs.en: Uhmmm, it is heterogeneous due to feeling like extra-super competent.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese explains that her difference lies in being far too extraordinarily capable. The English retains the inapplicable technical adjective and uses a malformed causal phrase ending in 'competent.'
ghs.remedy: She's different because she is simply far too capable.

highlights.text: heterogeneous due to feeling like extra-super competent

rows.jp: 失敗がない人間って、どうなんでしょう？
rows.en: What were we to make of someone who never failed?

ghs.en: What does one do about humans that have no failings?

rows.jp: 失敗する率が極端に低い人間って、言葉にするとそれだけですが。
rows.en: Put into words, that was all she was: someone with a vanishingly low failure rate.

ghs.en: Well, once it has been put into words, it is merely a human with an extremely low probability of failure.

rows.jp: 普通の人が百回死ぬような事態に二百回生存しちゃうげな。
rows.en: In a situation that would kill a normal person a hundred times over, she’d survive two hundred times.

ghs.en: Like in a situation where a normal person would die a hundred times, they'd survive two hundred times.

rows.jp: そりゃほとんどアータ！　ホーリーウッドの一時間四十五分時点の主人公の性能ですよ。
rows.en: Why, that's practically the power of a Holywood hero at the one-hour-forty-five-minute mark!

ghs.en: That is almost like an ah'tress! That is the performance of a Holywood protagonist at the one hour, forty-five minutes mark!

rows.jp: ラスト十分前が一番性能が高いわけですな。
rows.en: A hero reached peak performance ten minutes before the end, you see.

ghs.en: Before the last ten minutes, their performances are at the absolute highest, indeed.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that a protagonist's abilities peak during the ten minutes before the ending. The English says they peak before that final ten-minute interval begins.
ghs.remedy: In the final ten minutes

rows.jp: そこで考えた、アンチ映画。
rows.en: Which gave me an idea: the anti-movie.

ghs.en: And with that I thought: anti-movie.

rows.jp: ラスト十分まで昼寝しまくって、最後に超人モードになって敵を倒すストーリー。
rows.en: The hero naps until the last ten minutes, enters superhuman mode, and defeats the enemy.

ghs.en: A story where until the last ten minutes he does nothing but take naps, then at the end he goes into Hyperman Mode and defeats the bad guy.

rows.jp: あとまったく脈絡なくもう一つ考えた。
rows.en: Then, for no reason at all, I thought of another one.

ghs.en: And then without a damn trace of logical connection I had one more idea:

rows.jp: 人類滅亡からはじまるストーリー。
rows.en: A story that begins with the extinction of humanity.

ghs.en: a story that has its beginning with the Fall of Mankind.

rows.jp: これやん。
rows.en: That's this story.

ghs.en: That, yah.

rows.jp: まさに俺って感じだ。
rows.en: Now that was me all over.

ghs.en: Really feels me-ish.

rows.jp: 自分賛美歌。
rows.en: A hymn to myself.

ghs.en: It's a hymn to the self.

rows.jp: 人を貶めることで自分を高める行為とどっちが卑しいだろう？
rows.en: Which was more contemptible: praising myself, or putting others down to lift myself up?

ghs.en: But which is vulgar now, that or making oneself great by tearing down others?

rows.jp: そこいらどうなんだろう？
rows.en: How did that work, anyway?

ghs.en: Well, what do we do about that?

rows.jp: 俺は問いかけた。
rows.en: I posed the question.

ghs.en: I asked out.
ghs.assessment: 問いかける means that Taichi posed the question. 'Asked out' means inviting someone on a date and lacks an object here.
ghs.remedy: I posed the question.

rows.jp: 「ブライダルお姫様だっこ」
rows.en: “Bridal princess carry.”

ghs.en: Youko: "Bridal princess carry."

rows.jp: すっげ哲学的。まいった。勝てない。
rows.en: Damn. Deep. She had me beat. I couldn't compete.

ghs.en: Waaay philosophical. Bummer. I can't beat this.

rows.jp: もうっ、カメラ返せよ！
rows.en: Come on! Give me back the camera!

ghs.en: Awww, give me my camera back now!

rows.jp: 誰と遊ぼう？
rows.en: Who should I play with?

ghs.en: Who do I play with?

rows.jp: じゃ、みみ先輩だ。
rows.en: Mimi it is, then.

ghs.en: Yeah, Mimi-senpai.

rows.jp: 寝てるよ！
rows.en: She’s asleep!

ghs.en: She's asleep!

rows.jp: 起きたあっ！？
rows.en: She woke up!?

ghs.en: She woke uuup?!

rows.jp: 「モラルの欠如、行きすぎた利己的な個人主義、自分が怠惰に過ごすために利用される基本的人権、このようないい子ハザードによって汚染されている現代社会に――」
rows.en: “Modern society has been contaminated by moral bankruptcy, rampant selfish individualism, and fundamental human rights invoked merely as a license for indolence—by what I call the Goody-Goody Hazard—”

ghs.en:
Misato: "A deficiency in morals, an exaggerated
selfish individualism, the utilization of
fundamental human rights for the purpose of
overindulging oneself in laziness: are youthful
ones like you and me still capable of making
friends with which to grow each other in a modern
society polluted by that sort of Nice Children
Hazards? It is my conviction that our Gunjou
Institute Broadcast Club can possibly tender
a satisfactory response to that question!"

rows.jp: 「私たち若者は互いに築き上げる交友を持つことができるのでしょうか？　我が群青学院放送部は、この疑問に対して満足のゆく答えを提供することができると考えています」
rows.en: “Can we, the youth of today, still forge friendships that build each other up? Gunjo Academy Broadcasting Club believes it can provide a satisfactory answer to this question.”

rows.jp: うへえ！
rows.en: Ugh!

ghs.en: Uweeeh!

rows.jp: 大きく出たな。
rows.en: Talk about aiming high.

ghs.en: A big one came out!
ghs.assessment: 大きく出た means that Misato made an audacious or grand claim. The English literalizes size and emergence as a large object coming out.
ghs.remedy: That's a bold claim!

rows.jp: さすがみみみ先輩。
rows.en: That's Mimimi for you.

ghs.en: What else from Mimimi-senpai.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means 'just what you'd expect from Mimimi-senpai.' The English omits the verb and uses an opaque rhetorical fragment.
ghs.remedy: Just what you'd expect from Mimimi-senpai.

rows.jp: この人の弱さってのは、なんかおっぱいの感触と似てる。
rows.en: There's something about her weakness that feels like the softness of her breasts.

ghs.en: The weakness of this person sort of resembles the tactile sensation of boobs.

rows.jp: だから大好きというのが本音だ。
rows.en: And honestly, that's why I love her.

ghs.en: Therefore great love is the true intent here.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says frankly that this is why he loves her. The English turns his feeling into the abstract subject 'great love' and his candid admission into an unspecified intent.
ghs.remedy: That's why I love her, honestly.

highlights.text: Therefore great love is the true intent here.

rows.jp: 実は好きでも何でもない。
rows.en: Actually, I don't even like her.

ghs.en: Truth is, love's sorta whatever.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese bluntly retracts the claim: in truth, he does not like her at all. The English instead expresses vague indifference toward love as a concept.
ghs.remedy: Actually, I don't like her at all.

rows.jp: 好きになるって設定上で定めただけだ。
rows.en: I just wrote 'falls for her' into my character settings.

ghs.en: That we'd fall in love is just something established by the scenario's Settei.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says only that the setting defines him as liking her. The English makes the love mutual, invents a scenario as possessor, and leaves 設定 as an unexplained capitalized loanword.
ghs.remedy: The setting merely says that I'm supposed to like her.

rows.jp: ごめんなさい。
rows.en: I’m sorry.

ghs.en: Apologies.

rows.jp: やさぐれちゃったよ！！
rows.en: She's turned into a delinquent!!

ghs.en: She's sulking now!!!

rows.jp: そんなに『みみみ』呼ばわりはイヤなのかよ！
rows.en: Does she really hate being called 'Mimimi' that much!?

ghs.en: Is that how much she hates to be called "Mimimi"?!

rows.jp: 超可愛いのになぁ。
rows.en: It’s super cute, though.

ghs.en: C'mon, but it's Hyper Kawaii...

rows.jp: ちぇっ。
rows.en: Tch.

ghs.en: Tsk.

rows.jp: とすると美希だな。
rows.en: Miki, then.

ghs.en: Let's follow that up with Miki then.

rows.jp: 慰めてもらうしか。
rows.en: She'll have to console me.

ghs.en: I get nothing but consolation.
ghs.assessment: Taichi decides that he has no choice but to seek comfort from Miki. The English states that consolation is already the only thing he receives.
ghs.remedy: I'll have to get Miki to comfort me.

rows.jp: ぉぃぉぃ！
rows.en: H-hey!

ghs.en: (hey now!)

rows.jp: おいおい！
rows.en: Hey, hey!

ghs.en: HEY NOW!

rows.jp: 多重放送になった俺だ。
rows.en: I'd become a multiplex broadcast.

ghs.en: I ended up as a multiplex broadcast.

rows.jp: モノローグでだけどな。
rows.en: In monologue only, but still.

ghs.en: Only via monologue, though.

rows.jp: しっかし、すげえサービス精神旺盛な成果物だな。
rows.en: Still, talk about a product packed with fanservice.

ghs.en: Annnd yet, that's one finished delivered product that's chock full of that waaay amazing Service spirit!
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the work a product overflowing with eagerness to entertain or please. The English stacks redundant production adjectives and capitalizes an awkward calque as though it were a named doctrine.
ghs.remedy: That's one work packed with an incredible eagerness to please.

rows.jp: いいのか？
rows.en: Is this okay?

ghs.en: Is that OK?

rows.jp: 許されるのか？
rows.en: Are they allowed to do this?

ghs.en: Will that be permitted?

rows.jp: 認証されたのか？
rows.en: Was this approved?

ghs.en: Will it pass certification?

rows.jp: アダルト・カテゴリに入れるのか？
rows.en: Does it belong in the Adults Only section?

ghs.en: Will it be put in the Adults category?
ghs.assessment: The Japanese refers to the singular adult category. The English uses the plural personal noun 'Adults' as an attributive category name.
ghs.remedy: adult category

rows.jp: 「ごろにゃーごろ」
rows.en: “Purrrr-meow-purr.”

ghs.en: Miki: "Purr-meow-purr."

rows.jp: 猫語か！
rows.en: Cat language!

ghs.en: Catspeak?!

rows.jp: まいったな、履修してないぞ。
rows.en: Damn. I never took Cat as a foreign language.

ghs.en: I give up, I didn't study that.

rows.jp: 意思の疎通ができない。
rows.en: We can’t communicate.

ghs.en: Reciprocal understanding of intent is impossible.

rows.jp: ただ下着を見るだけの俺になってしまいそうだ。
rows.en: At this rate, I'll turn into a man who does nothing but stare at her panties.

ghs.en: It seems I ended up as someone who just looks at panties.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that at this rate Taichi is liable to become such a person. The English says that the transformation already happened and only now appears evident.
ghs.remedy: It looks as though I'll become

rows.jp: よしなろう。
rows.en: All right. That's what I'll become.

ghs.en: That'd be good thing to be.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese is Taichi's immediate resolution: 'All right, I'll become one.' The English turns it into a hypothetical evaluation and omits the article before 'good thing.'
ghs.remedy: All right, I'll become one.

highlights.text: That'd be good thing to be.

rows.jp: 俺はおよそ十四時間、下着を凝視した。
rows.en: I stared at her panties for approximately fourteen hours.

ghs.en: And I, for roughly fourteen hours, fixed a stare on the underwear.

rows.jp: 時間にして四秒ほどの出来事だった。
rows.en: It all happened in about four seconds.

ghs.en: As far as time is concerned it was an event about four seconds long.

rows.jp: ありがとう美希。
rows.en: Thank you, Miki.

ghs.en: Thank you, Miki.

rows.jp: グンナイ。
rows.en: G’night.

ghs.en: GUNAI (good night).

rows.jp: 遊びのあとはレクリエーション。
rows.en: After playtime comes recreation.

ghs.en: After playing around we have recreation.

rows.jp: 部活に精を出す。
rows.en: I threw myself into club work.

ghs.en: I spurt forth my spirit in the club.
ghs.assessment: 精を出す is an idiom meaning to apply oneself diligently. The English turns effort into a bodily emission of spirit and adds sexualized physical imagery.
ghs.remedy: I throw myself into club work.

highlights.text: I spurt forth my spirit in the club.

rows.jp: エッチラオッチラ。
rows.en: Heave-ho, heave-ho.

ghs.en: Laboriously with a lot of sexfort.

rows.jp: 自動的に働く。
rows.en: I worked on autopilot.

ghs.en: Working automatically.

rows.jp: 人は誰だってなかば自動的なんだ。
rows.en: Everyone was at least half autopilot.

ghs.en: People, all of them, are semi-automatic.

rows.jp: それの、どこが悪い？
rows.en: What was wrong with that?

ghs.en: And what part of that, exactly, is bad?

rows.jp: 「退屈で、気が狂いそうになりますよ？」
rows.en: “You’ll go crazy from boredom, you know?”

ghs.en: Miki: "I would just lose my mind from boredom, wouldn't I?"

rows.jp: え？
rows.en: What?

ghs.en: Eh?

rows.jp: 「あ、だめ、だめですよっ！？」
rows.en: “No, wait—you can’t!”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Ah, you can't, you can't do that!"

rows.jp: だめって、何が？
rows.en: Couldn't what?

ghs.en: Can't, what exactly?

rows.jp: 空。
rows.en: Sky.

ghs.en: The sky,

rows.jp: そして。
rows.en: And then.

ghs.en: and then,

rows.jp: 地面。遙か下方。
rows.en: The ground. Far below.

ghs.en: the ground. Far, far below.

rows.jp: その瞬間。
rows.en: At that instant.

ghs.en: That instant,

rows.jp: 破裂―――
rows.en: Burst—

ghs.en: rupture---

rows.jp: 「あああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああああっ！！！！」
rows.en: “Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!!!!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!!!!!"

rows.jp: 語句の連結が外れてできた言葉の海から、俺は手を伸ばす。
rows.en: The links between phrases came apart, leaving me adrift in a sea of words. I reached out.

ghs.en: I stretch my hand out from the ocean of words that had managed to undo the connection with sentences.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes a sea of words formed when the connections among phrases came apart. The English makes words intentionally succeed at severing a connection they had 'with sentences' and does not identify the relations among the words themselves.
ghs.remedy: the sea of words left when the links between phrases came apart

highlights.text: words that had managed to undo the connection with sentences

rows.jp: 掴む藁もない。
rows.en: There wasn't even a straw to grasp at.

ghs.en: I grasp no straw.

rows.jp: くるりと意識を反転して（たこ焼きのように）現世に戻る。
rows.en: I flipped my consciousness over—like a takoyaki ball—and returned to the world of the living.

ghs.en: Suddenly spinning and covering myself in consciousness (like a takoyaki) I return to the present world.
ghs.assessment: Taichi flips his consciousness around like turning a takoyaki and returns to the present world. The English instead makes him spin bodily and wrap himself in consciousness.
ghs.remedy: I flip my consciousness over (like a takoyaki) and return to the present world.

highlights.text: spinning and covering myself in consciousness

rows.jp: 意識が現世を観測してのけた。
rows.en: My consciousness managed to Observe the world of the living.

ghs.en: Consciousness wrung to observing the present world.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that his consciousness successfully managed to observe the present world. The English uses 'wrung' without a coherent object or construction.
ghs.remedy: My consciousness managed to observe the present world.

highlights.text: Consciousness wrung to observing the present world.

rows.jp: 「はっ、はっ、はっ……」
rows.en: “Hah... hah... hah...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hah, hah, hah..."

rows.jp: 俺は、自ら破壊したフェンスから身を乗り出そうとしていた。
rows.en: I found myself trying to lean out through the hole I'd torn in the fence.

ghs.en: I had just about begun to lean myself out of the fence that I had wrecked by myself.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he was about to lean his body out through the opening in the fence. The English uses the transitive reflexive 'lean myself' and treats the fence as a container he is emerging from.
ghs.remedy: lean out through the opening in the fence

highlights.text: lean myself out of the fence

rows.jp: 強ばった指が、左右の金網をつかんでいる。
rows.en: My rigid fingers clutched the wire mesh on either side.

ghs.en: Stiffened fingers are grasping the wire mesh on the left and right.

rows.jp: ギリギリのところだったのだろう。
rows.en: I must have stopped myself just in time.

ghs.en: This was just barely the last moment indeed.

rows.jp: フェンスは扉大にくりぬかれていた。
rows.en: A doorway-sized hole had been cut through the fence.

ghs.en: The fence had been excavated into door size.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that a door-sized opening had been cut out of the fence. 'Excavated' refers to digging earth or removing buried material, and 'into door size' is ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: A door-sized opening had been cut out of the fence.

rows.jp: 俺がやった。その記憶がある。
rows.en: I had done it. I remembered that much.

ghs.en: My doing. I have the recollections of that.

rows.jp: 記憶するはしからズタズタに分断され、他の言語に混じって判断できなくなっていたんだ。
rows.en: The instant a memory formed, it was torn to shreds and mixed with other words until I couldn't tell one from another.

ghs.en: No sooner than they had been memorized they had been torn up into tiny pieces and mixed with other languages, that I could no longer decipher them.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that memories were shredded even as he formed them and mixed with other language until he could no longer judge them. The English changes remembering into deliberate memorization, pluralizes 'language,' and joins the result with an ungrammatical 'that.'
ghs.remedy: As soon as I formed a memory, it was torn apart and mixed with other language until I could no longer make sense of it.

highlights.text: No sooner than they had been memorized

rows.jp: 指先が石膏のように白い。
rows.en: My fingertips were white as plaster.

ghs.en: My fingertips are as white as plaster.

rows.jp: ずっと力んでいたせいか。
rows.en: Maybe I'd been gripping it that hard for that long.

ghs.en: Perhaps because they have been gripping all along.

rows.jp: 重心を背後に引き戻した。
rows.en: I shifted my weight back.

ghs.en: I restore my center of gravity to my back.
ghs.assessment: Taichi shifts his center of gravity backward to regain safety. The English treats his back as a location to which the center of gravity belongs or returns.
ghs.remedy: I shift my center of gravity backward.

highlights.text: restore my center of gravity to my back

rows.jp: これで安全。落ちない。
rows.en: Safe. I wouldn't fall now.

ghs.en: This is safe. I won't fall.

rows.jp: なおフェンスに食い込んでいる指。苦労してはがす。
rows.en: My fingers were still dug into the wire. I struggled to pry them loose.

ghs.en: Still the fingertips eat down into the fence. I peel off with difficulty.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that his fingers are still digging into the fence and that he painfully peels them away. The English personifies the fingertips as eating downward and omits the object of 'peel off.'
ghs.remedy: My fingers are still dug into the fence. I struggle to peel them away.

highlights.text: the fingertips eat down into the fence. I peel off

rows.jp: 軽い苦痛。
rows.en: A dull ache.

ghs.en: Mild pain.

rows.jp: 裏返すと、うっすらと網目状に血が浮いていた。
rows.en: When I turned my hands over, a faint grid of blood showed beneath the skin.

ghs.en: When I turn them upside down, blood was surfacing in a reticulate.
ghs.assessment: When he turns his hands over, faint blood rises in a mesh pattern. The English shifts tense, uses the adjective 'reticulate' as an incomplete count noun, and omits the pattern's visible form.
ghs.remedy: faint blood had risen in a mesh pattern

highlights.text: blood was surfacing in a reticulate

ghs.en: Taichi: "I...
ghs.assessment: The English dialogue opens a quotation mark but never closes it.
ghs.remedy: Taichi: "I..."

rows.jp: 自殺しようとしたことが、信じられない。
rows.en: I could not believe I had tried to kill myself.

ghs.en: I can't believe it, I was trying to commit suicide.
ghs.assessment: The English joins two independent clauses with a comma and makes 'it' an unexplained object before restating the actual fact.
ghs.remedy: I can't believe I was trying

highlights.text: I can't believe it, I was trying

rows.jp: 死んではいけない。
rows.en: I couldn't die.

ghs.en: Death is out of the question.

rows.jp: たくさん殺して、生きたのだから。
rows.en: Not after killing so many and living through it.

ghs.en: Because you made a living by killing so much.
ghs.assessment: Taichi tells himself that he killed many and nevertheless lived, which is why he must not die now. The English shifts to second person and turns survival after killing into earning a livelihood through killing.
ghs.remedy: Because I've killed so many and survived.

highlights.text: you made a living by killing so much

rows.jp: 「そうなんだろ……曜子ちゃん？」
rows.en: “That's right... isn't it, Youko?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't that right... Youko-chan?"

rows.jp: 呼んでも、彼女はあらわれない。
rows.en: I called her name, but she didn't appear.

ghs.en: I call her, but the girl does not turn up.

rows.jp: 自分を抱きしめる。
rows.en: I wrapped my arms around myself.

ghs.en: I hug myself.

rows.jp: 寒い。
rows.en: I was cold.

ghs.en: So cold.

rows.jp: いてもたってもいられなくなる。
rows.en: I couldn't sit still.

ghs.en: I become unable to sit still.

rows.jp: 走り出す。
rows.en: I started running.

ghs.en: I start to run.

rows.jp: 校内に。
rows.en: Into the school.

ghs.en: Inside the school building.

rows.jp: 「うわあああああああああああああっ」
rows.en: “Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "WAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"

rows.jp: 駆ける。
rows.en: I ran.

ghs.en: I dash.

rows.jp: 人！
rows.en: Someone!

ghs.en: People!

rows.jp: 人！
rows.en: Someone!

ghs.en: People!

rows.jp: どっかに人！
rows.en: Someone, somewhere!

ghs.en: Anywhere, people!
ghs.assessment: Taichi desperately calls for any person to be somewhere. The English reverses the order into an ungrammatical location-plus-plural fragment.
ghs.remedy: Someone! Anywhere!

rows.jp: 「美希、霧！」
rows.en: “Miki! Kiri!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Miki, Kiri!"

rows.jp: いない。
rows.en: No one.

ghs.en: Not here.

rows.jp: 机を倒していく。
rows.en: I sent desks crashing over as I ran.

ghs.en: I throw around the desks.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that he knocks desks over as he proceeds. 'Throw around' suggests lifting and hurling them in multiple directions.
ghs.remedy: knock over the desks

rows.jp: どんどん倒していく。
rows.en: One after another.

ghs.en: Knock them down one after the other.

rows.jp: 教科書が床に滑り落ちる。
rows.en: Textbooks slid onto the floor.

ghs.en: Textbooks slip down to the ground.
ghs.assessment: The textbooks slide onto the interior floor. 'Ground' normally denotes outdoor earth or terrain.
ghs.remedy: to the floor

rows.jp: 二人はいない。
rows.en: Neither of them was there.

ghs.en: The two are not among us.

rows.jp: 恐怖。
rows.en: Terror.

ghs.en: Terror.

rows.jp: この空間には誰もいない。
rows.en: There was no one in this space.

ghs.en: In this room there is no one.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese expands the realization to this entire space, not merely the current room. The English narrows the absence to one room.
ghs.remedy: In this whole space

rows.jp: 逃げ出す。
rows.en: I fled.

ghs.en: I run away.

rows.jp: 長細い空間。
rows.en: A long, narrow corridor.

ghs.en: A thin and narrow space.
ghs.assessment: 長細い describes a long, narrow space. The English replaces length with thinness and then redundantly adds narrowness.
ghs.remedy: A long, narrow space.

rows.jp: 挟み撃ちにされたら助からないという危機感。
rows.en: A sudden fear that if something came at me from both ends, I wouldn't stand a chance.

ghs.en: A sense of impeding danger that says I would never survive should I be subjected to a pincer attack.
ghs.assessment: The intended word is 'impending,' not 'impeding,' and the internal warning does not literally speak a proposition.
ghs.remedy: impending danger: I would never survive

rows.jp: 敵は虚無だ。
rows.en: My enemy was the void.

ghs.en: The enemy are the Nihil.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese personifies a single abstract enemy: the void or nothingness. The English pluralizes it, uses plural agreement, and invents the proper collective name 'the Nihil.'
ghs.remedy: The enemy is the void.

rows.jp: 奴らはどこにでもいる。
rows.en: The void was everywhere.

ghs.en: Those bastards are everywhere.

rows.jp: もう俺を包んでいる。
rows.en: It was already closing around me.

ghs.en: By now they are engulfing me.

rows.jp: このままでは俺は拡散して、希薄になってしまう。
rows.en: At this rate, I'd diffuse, growing thinner and thinner.

ghs.en: If I keep this up I will spread, and end up diluted.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that if the surrounding condition continues, Taichi will diffuse. The English implies that his own continuing behavior causes the danger.
ghs.remedy: If this keeps up

rows.jp: 階段を通過し、二年教室。
rows.en: Past the stairs. The second-year classrooms.

ghs.en: I pass through the staircase to the Second Years' classroom.
ghs.assessment: Taichi goes via the stairs to a second-year classroom. A staircase is traversed along, not passed through, and the English invents a capitalized plural possessive name.
ghs.remedy: I take the stairs to a second-year classroom.

rows.jp: 冬子の個室。
rows.en: Touko's private room.

ghs.en: Touko's private room.

rows.jp: 周囲と隔絶された小さな要塞だった。
rows.en: A tiny fortress cut off from everything around it.

ghs.en: A tiny fortress, separated from its surroundings.

rows.jp: けど主がいない。
rows.en: But its master was gone.

ghs.en: But its master is not here.

rows.jp: 強ばった意志とともに送還された。
rows.en: Sent back along with her unyielding will.

ghs.en: She was sent back together with her stiff determination.

rows.jp: でも少しくらいいてくれてもいいじゃないか。
rows.en: Still, couldn't she have stayed just a little longer?

ghs.en: But wouldn't it have been nice if she had stayed here for just a little more?

rows.jp: 「ああああああっ、ああああああああッッッ！！」
rows.en: “Aaaaaah! Aaaaaaaaaaah!!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "AAAAAAH, AAAAAAAAHHH!!!"

rows.jp: こけつまろびつ、門をまたぐ。
rows.en: Stumbling and scrambling, I passed through the gate.

ghs.en: Running and falling and stumbling I fly across the gate.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that Taichi crosses the gate while stumbling and tumbling. The English invents flight and uses 'across' for passing a gate boundary.
ghs.remedy: I stumble and tumble through the gate.

rows.jp: 俺は街中を彷徨う。
rows.en: I wandered the streets.

ghs.en: I roam downtown,
ghs.assessment: 街中 means throughout the town or city. 'Downtown' restricts the search to a central commercial district.
ghs.remedy: through the town

rows.jp: 生者を捜して。
rows.en: Looking for anyone alive.

ghs.en: in search of the living.

rows.jp: そもそも交差世界の残滓でしかないここに、もともと生者がいたのかどうか。
rows.en: Had anyone living ever existed here to begin with, in this mere residue of the cross-world?

ghs.en: Whether or not these dregs of a crossed world that these are, and nothing more, ever held the living in the first place.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese wonders whether living people ever existed in this place, which is only the residue of intersecting worlds. The English duplicates 'these,' leaves a relative clause without a predicate, and turns the local place into plural dregs as the container.
ghs.remedy: Did living people ever exist here in the first place, in a place that is only the residue of intersecting worlds?

highlights.text: Whether or not these dregs of a crossed world that these are, and nothing more, ever held the living in the first place.

rows.jp: けど捜さずにはいられない。
rows.en: But I had to keep looking.

ghs.en: But I cannot but search.

rows.jp: 人を求めずにはいられない。
rows.en: I had to keep searching for someone.

ghs.en: I cannot but seek people.

rows.jp: 「あ……はぁ、はっ……ッ」
rows.en: “Ah... hah... hah...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah... haah, hah...!"

rows.jp: 一軒一軒、家を確かめていく。
rows.en: I checked the houses one by one.

ghs.en: Building by building I examine the houses.

rows.jp: 狂乱の半日。
rows.en: Half a day in a frenzy.

ghs.en: For a half day of madness,

rows.jp: 俺は求め続けた。
rows.en: Still I searched.

ghs.en: I continued to seek.

rows.jp: 門の前で、へたる。
rows.en: At the gate, I collapsed.

ghs.en: In front of the gate I lose my strength.

rows.jp: 「……ったくなぁ……一人もいねー」
rows.en: “...Damn... not one.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...'mmit now... there's nobodyyy!"
ghs.assessment: The Japanese frustrated filler is roughly 'honestly' or 'damn.' The English creates the malformed clipped string ''mmit.'
ghs.remedy: damn it

rows.jp: どんだけ捜しても。
rows.en: No matter how hard I searched.

ghs.en: Howevermuch whateverway I search,
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means 'no matter how hard I looked.' The English fuses 'however much' into one word and adds the nonexistent compound 'whateverway.'
ghs.remedy: No matter how hard I looked

rows.jp: もう誰もいないのだった。
rows.en: There was no one left.

ghs.en: there was no one anymore anywhere.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that nobody was left. The English stacks three negative scope expressions without idiomatic ordering.
ghs.remedy: there was no one left anywhere

rows.jp: けど疲労と引き替えに、少し、落ち着いた。
rows.en: But I had traded exhaustion for a little calm.

ghs.en: But in exchange for all this fatigue I had calmed down, just a bit.

rows.jp: 激しい運動をするため、脳が用いられたためだろうか？
rows.en: Maybe all that exertion had forced my brain to work?

ghs.en: It's because to make strenuous movements I needed to make use of the brain, right?
ghs.assessment: Taichi wonders whether he calmed down because strenuous exercise occupied or used his brain. The English says he deliberately needed his brain in order to produce movement and uses the count noun 'movements.'
ghs.remedy: Maybe because strenuous exercise occupied my brain?

highlights.text: to make strenuous movements I needed to make use of the brain

rows.en: “Ah.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah."

rows.jp: そうだ。
rows.en: That was it.

ghs.en: That's right.

rows.jp: 突き動かされて、山に。
rows.en: Something drove me up the mountain.

ghs.en: Stimulated, I head to the mountains.
ghs.assessment: 突き動かされて means driven or compelled by an inner impulse. 'Stimulated' suggests mere arousal or increased activity.
ghs.remedy: Driven by an impulse

rows.jp: 目を疑った。
rows.en: I could not believe my eyes.

ghs.en: I couldn't believe my eyes.

rows.jp: なにもない？
rows.en: Nothing?

ghs.en: There's nothing here?

rows.jp: あのぼやけた不確定な理解不能空間は、きれいさっぱり消失していた。
rows.en: That blurred, uncertain, incomprehensible space had vanished cleanly and completely.

ghs.en: That blurry, indeterminably incomprehensible space had vanished without a trace.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese coordinates the space as blurry, indeterminate, and incomprehensible. The English turns 'indeterminate' into an adverb modifying incomprehensibility.
ghs.remedy: blurry, indeterminate, incomprehensible

rows.jp: 「……馬鹿な」
rows.en: “No way.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...that's absurd."

rows.jp: 何千週と存在し続けたものじゃないのか？
rows.en: Hadn't it been there for thousands of weeks?

ghs.en: Hasn't this thing continued to exist for many thousands of weeks?

rows.jp: いや、万かも知れない。
rows.en: Maybe tens of thousands.

ghs.en: Nah, it might even be tens of thousand.
ghs.assessment: The quantified count noun requires the plural 'thousands.'
ghs.remedy: tens of thousands

rows.jp: 「どうしてなくなるんだよ」
rows.en: “Why would it disappear?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why has it gone now!"

rows.jp: 憤り。
rows.en: Anger.

ghs.en: Resentment.

rows.jp: 絶望。
rows.en: Despair.

ghs.en: Desperation.
ghs.assessment: 絶望 is despair or hopelessness. 'Desperation' is an urgent drive to act under extreme pressure and does not preserve the loss of hope.
ghs.remedy: Despair.

rows.jp: 名状できない感情。
rows.en: An emotion without a name.

ghs.en:
Feelings I am incapable
of describing.

rows.jp: 痛み。
rows.en: Pain.

ghs.en: Pain.

rows.jp: 心からもたらされるものに束縛され、俺は立ちすくんだ。
rows.en: I stood frozen, shackled by everything welling up from my heart.

ghs.en: Shackled by what is brought out from the bottom of my heart I stood, petrified.

rows.jp: 「どうして……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why..."

rows.jp: 逃げたい。
rows.en: I wanted to run.

ghs.en: I want to run away.

rows.jp: あたりまえの感情。
rows.en: The most natural feeling there was.

ghs.en: An everyday emotion.

rows.jp: 必死で養った、俺のちっぽけな心にもそれはあった。
rows.en: Even my tiny heart—the one I'd struggled so desperately to nurture—could feel it.

ghs.en: It existed in this frantically cultivated, worthlessly tiny heart of mine as well.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese calls the heart tiny but says Taichi nurtured it desperately. The English changes desperate effort to frantic cultivation and adds the judgment that the heart is worthless.
ghs.remedy: the tiny heart I had desperately nurtured

rows.jp: みみ先輩、
rows.en: Mimi,

ghs.en:
Mimi-senpai,
Tomoki,
Kiri,
Miki,
Youko-chan...

rows.jp: 友貴、
rows.en: Tomoki,

rows.jp: 霧、
rows.en: Kiri,

rows.jp: 美希、
rows.en: Miki,

rows.jp: 曜子ちゃん……。
rows.en: Youko...

rows.jp: みんなことを、とても笑えない。
rows.en: I couldn't laugh at any of them. Not now.

ghs.en: I can't really laugh at all you guys.

rows.jp: けれどゲートはもうない。
rows.en: But the gate was gone.

ghs.en: However the gate is no more.

rows.jp: 帰りたくても帰れない。
rows.en: Even if I wanted to go back, I couldn't.

ghs.en: I can't go home even if I want to go home.

rows.jp: 補正する『ずれ』はなくなったんだ。
rows.en: There was no ‘misalignment’ left to correct.

ghs.en: Correction: the 'shift' was no more.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the discrepancy which might have been corrected no longer exists. The English turns 'correction' into an editorial label and merely says the shift is gone, obscuring its role as the object of correction.
ghs.remedy: There was no longer any 'discrepancy' left to correct.

rows.jp: 一人。
rows.en: Alone.

ghs.en: Alone.

rows.jp: 交差した世界。
rows.en: A world that had intersected another.

ghs.en: In a world that has crossed,

rows.jp: 交差するのは一点で。
rows.en: They had touched at a single point.

ghs.en: the crossing is at one single point.

rows.jp: それぞれの流れは、また続いていく。
rows.en: Then each current continued on its way.

ghs.en: Their respective flows are still continuing.

rows.jp: 「ああ……そうか」
rows.en: “Ah... I see.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh... that's right."

rows.jp: 俺のいるこの虚無の街は……もう―――
rows.en: This empty city I was in had already—

ghs.en: This town of nihility where I now live... is now---

rows.jp: 交差点を過ぎたんだ。
rows.en: passed the intersection.

ghs.en: Past its point of crossing.

rows.jp: 『Ｘ』の字を想定してみればわかる。
rows.en: Picture the letter X.

ghs.en: Understandable if looking at the very character "X".
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says that the idea becomes clear if one imagines the shape of the letter X. The English supplies neither the person who understands nor an idiomatic conditional construction.
ghs.remedy: You can see it if you picture the letter X.

highlights.text: Understandable if looking at the very character "X".

rows.jp: 二本の棒。それぞれの流れ。
rows.en: Two strokes. Two separate flows.

ghs.en: Two lines. Their respective flows continuing.

rows.jp: 一瞬の交差。だが流れは止まらないわけだ。
rows.en: One moment of crossing. But neither flow stopped.

ghs.en: The crossing is an instant. Yet the flows don't stop.

rows.jp: 俺はもう一本の流れに乗ったのか？
rows.en: Had I been swept into the other flow?

ghs.en: Did I ride a third flow here?
ghs.assessment: The passage has established two intersecting flows. もう一本 asks whether Taichi moved onto the other or another one, not a third flow.
ghs.remedy: Did I move onto the other flow?

rows.jp: いや……違うだろう。
rows.en: No... that wasn't it.

ghs.en: Nah... gotta be something else.

rows.jp: 今の街は、残滓だ。
rows.en: The city now was only residue.

ghs.en: This town, now, is just the dregs.

rows.jp: 流れゆく二本の残像の交差点。
rows.en: The intersection where two passing afterimages had met.

ghs.en: The afterimage of the Cross Point of two continuing flows.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese describes the present town as the point where two flowing afterimages intersect. The English instead makes the Cross Point itself an afterimage and leaves an isolated noun phrase whose relations are unclear.
ghs.remedy: The intersection of two afterimages flowing onward.

highlights.text: The afterimage of the Cross Point of two continuing flows.

rows.jp: 『実』が過ぎ去り『虚』になったクロスポイント。
rows.en: A cross-point left ‘Unreal’ after the ‘Real’ moved on.

ghs.en: A Cross Point where Real has passed by and became Imaginary.
ghs.assessment: The coordinated perfect construction requires 'has become,' while the source describes the completed transition from real to unreal.
ghs.remedy: has passed by and become

ghs.en: Taichi: "...hahah."

rows.jp: 「ははは」
rows.en: “Ha ha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahahah."

rows.jp: 「はははははははははははははっ」
rows.en: “Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hahahahahahahahahahahahahah!"

rows.jp: この笑いは。
rows.en: This laughter was—

ghs.en: This laugh is,

rows.jp: 祝福。
rows.en: a blessing.

ghs.en: a blessing.

rows.jp: ゲートが消えるまで、どれだけの時間がかかったのか知れない。
rows.en: I had no idea how much time it had taken for the gate to disappear.

ghs.en: How much time it had passed before the gate had disappeared, I have no idea.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese says he does not know how much time elapsed before the gate disappeared. The English gives impersonal 'time' an expletive 'it' and uses an unnecessary past perfect for the elapsed time.
ghs.remedy: How much time passed before the gate disappeared

highlights.text: How much time it had passed before the gate had disappeared

rows.jp: けっこう早かったのかも。
rows.en: Maybe it had happened surprisingly fast.

ghs.en: Maybe it was kinda quick.

rows.jp: けど気の遠くなる年月だったのかも。
rows.en: Or maybe a dizzying stretch of years had passed.

ghs.en: But maybe it was a number of months and years that would boggle the mind.

rows.jp: どっちにしても、俺は堪え忍んだ。
rows.en: Either way, I'd held out.

ghs.en: Whichever it is, I will have to patiently endure this.
ghs.assessment: The Japanese states that, whichever duration was true, Taichi endured it. The English changes the completed endurance into a future obligation.
ghs.remedy: Either way, I endured it.

highlights.text: I will have to patiently endure this.

rows.jp: 逃げ場が遠のくほどの時を、闘い抜いた。
rows.en: I'd fought until my escape itself receded beyond reach.

ghs.en: In times when the place of refuge grows farther, the struggle is to the bitter end.
ghs.assessment: Taichi says that he fought his way through a span of time so long that escape receded into the distance. The English makes this a general present-tense maxim, removes him as subject, and turns duration into plural occasions.
ghs.remedy: I fought through a stretch of time long enough for escape itself to recede into the distance.

highlights.text: In times when the place of refuge grows farther, the struggle is to the bitter end.

rows.jp: 勝った。
rows.en: I won.

ghs.en: I won.

rows.jp: それだけは確かじゃないか。
rows.en: That much was certain, wasn’t it?

ghs.en: That alone is certain, isn't it.

rows.jp: 「逃げ場がないなら……生きるしか……ないもんな……」
rows.en: “If there's nowhere left to run... then I have no choice... but to live...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If I have no place of refuge... outside of living on... I've nothing... nothing..."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese means that if there is nowhere to run, he has no choice but to live. The English substitutes 'outside of living on,' leaves the construction without a coherent complement, and repeats an unsupported 'nothing.'
ghs.remedy: If there's nowhere to run... then I've got no choice... but to live...

highlights.text: If I have no place of refuge... outside of living on... I've nothing... nothing...

rows.jp: これでいい。
rows.en: This was enough.

ghs.en: That is good.

rows.jp: 「ざまあみろ、だ」
rows.en: “Serves you right.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Just dessert, yes."

rows.jp: トゥルー俺、ざまあみろ。
rows.en: True Me, serves you right.

ghs.en: Just dessert, oh true self.
ghs.assessment: The repeated ざまあみろ is again a taunt addressed to the 'true me.' The English replaces it with a misspelled and contextually different idiom.
ghs.remedy: Serves you right, true me.

rows.jp: おまえは（俺は）ここで飼い殺し。
rows.en: You'll (I'll) be left to rot here alive.

ghs.en: You shall (I shall) be kept here until you die.
Taichi: "......hahah."

rows.jp: 胸中、無数の感情が交錯し十字を描く。
rows.en: Countless emotions intersected inside my chest, tracing a cross.

ghs.en: Within my chest, emotions without number blend in shape cruciform.

rows.jp: 編み上げられる、架空のタペストリー。
rows.en: An imaginary tapestry woven into being.

ghs.en: An Air tapestry is being knit.
ghs.assessment: 架空 means imaginary or fictitious here. The English turns it into the capitalized noun 'Air,' and the progressive passive reads as a new action rather than the appositive image in the source.
ghs.remedy: An imaginary tapestry, woven together.
